assessment: The incumbent coordinates named groups, room reservations and staffed key collection while supporting telephone and in-person access. Repeating 90-minute bookings plausibly support predictability, but that benefit was not measured. Eleven groups obtained weekly bookings; administration exceeded two hours in two observed weeks, and three access conflicts occurred. The limiting observation is that 68% aggregate reservation coverage does not establish usable spare capacity: six declined requests targeted Tuesday or Thursday evenings, acceptable alternatives were unrecorded, and only one room has a piano. Missing needs and equipment data prevent assessing the 90% target or attributing unmet demand to scheduling alone.

openings.claim: Would assigning existing capacity against complete acceptable windows and equipment requirements meet demand, or do compatible requests exceed capacity?
openings.delta: Distinguishes recoverable allocation mismatch from scarcity at specific times and in the piano room; aggregate vacancy and lateness cannot distinguish these explanations.
openings.prediction: An allocation mismatch would permit a feasible reassignment that meets at least 90% of stated needs and every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement; a compatible-capacity bottleneck would leave identifiable overlapping demands unsatisfied even after reassignment.
openings.probe: Use each contact's short conversation to record weekly needs, acceptable windows, minimum useful duration and necessary equipment. Attempt a paper allocation within the existing rooms and hours, preserving the dated performances and weekly entitlement. Count only usable building rehearsal time; undocumented outside rehearsals do not establish success. Include conversation and scheduling time in administration totals.
assumptions: Contacts can state their groups' needs accurately.
Feasibility on paper requires later confirmation through attendance and access records.

openings.claim: A single authoritative reservation ledger with explicit read-back of each booking or change may reduce conflicting room expectations.
openings.delta: Addresses the observed calendar disagreement while testing whether the other double-arrival conflicts also originate in recording or confirmation failures.
openings.prediction: If inconsistent reservation state drives conflicts, double expectations should decline after ledger reconciliation and confirmation; conflicts despite matching confirmed entries would implicate other causes.
openings.probe: Keep telephone and desk changes available. Record each accepted change once in the authoritative paper ledger, read back room, date and time, and mark the online copy's update time. Over eight weeks record conflicts, whether confirmations agreed, and total administration minutes; judge against fewer than two conflicts and the two-hour weekly average.
assumptions: Staff can consult the authoritative ledger when issuing keys.
Confirmation and copying can fit the administration budget; this remains to be measured.
This change retains existing equipment, fees, opening hours, performances and weekly access entitlements.
